_comment: Port forwards carried by the background tunnels (Port Forwards window).
Compiled into the binary at build time — edit this file and rebuild.
THE BUILD FAILS IF NO FORWARDS ARE DECLARED HERE, and names what is
wrong. At runtime a malformed or empty file yields NO forwards rather
than an error — deliberately, so a bad config can never block a VS Code
launch — which means a stray comma, a quoted port or an empty
environments block all silently disable everything and look exactly
like a site that has no forwards. Nothing downstream can tell those
apart, so build.rs checks the file where it can still be shouted about.
`ALLOW_NO_FORWARDS=1` (or `./scripts/build_binaries.sh test`) builds a
development binary with none declared; it forwards nothing.
FILLING IT IN — copy a block out of _example_environments below into
environments, rename the key, and edit the entries.
key   the instance's MMODAL_ENV tag, matched case-insensitively.
ip    loopback address bound on THIS machine. Used only when your
hosts file has no entry for `host`; where it does, that IP wins
and this is ignored, so an existing hosts setup keeps working.
host  the remote DNS name. Resolved on the bastion, not locally.
port  optional. Omit it and the port comes from port_rules below.
EVERY ENVIRONMENT'S TUNNEL RUNS AT ONCE, so no two environments may
share an ip:port. The second ssh cannot bind it, and tunnels run with
ExitOnForwardFailure=yes, so that whole environment goes down. The app
detects this at startup and drops the clashing forward from the
alphabetically later environment, but the fix is distinct addresses:
give each environment its own /24, e.g. 127.200.10.x, 127.200.20.x.
Anything in 127.0.0.0/8 is loopback on Windows and needs no setup.
port_rules are checked IN ORDER and the FIRST match wins, so a name
like kafka-postgres-proxy takes the port of whichever rule is listed
first. Add a service type here rather than porting every entry.
A service on a non-standard port MUST have a rule here, or it silently
gets default_port and the forward is broken in a way that looks fine:
the local bind succeeds, so the window reports the ports forwarded,
and only a request through the tunnel finds that nothing answers.
Take those ports from a LocalForward line that is known to work, NOT
from vault_addr in accounts.json — that file ships as template data
(vault.dev1.YOUR-COMPANY.com:8200) and its ports describe nobody's
deployment. A vault rule of 8200 was added on that basis and broke a
site whose Vault sits behind 443, which is why there is no vault rule
here: it reaches the default like any other web service.
The hosts file is optional and is only ever read. With no entry a
forward still works, reached at its IP (https://127.200.20.1) instead
of by name; the app offers the lines to paste in when any are missing.

_example_environments._note: Examples only — this key is ignored. Copy into environments.
